text:
julia: FYI — vendor reported a perf/regression cluster on A100 when running our quantized kernels with CUDA 12.2. Looks like it's triggered only when driver is newer than 535.x and when images didn't pin the kernel ABI. Need rapid preflight for a targeted hotpatch + marketplace AMI rebuild.
lee: ack. Do we have a simple repro or telemetry link? /cc @carlos @maya
julia: repro snippet below, small run in perf lab. Happens ~15% of shorter sequence workloads.
```bash
# repro (lab)
python -m perf_runner --model q4_k --seq 128 --device a100 --cuda 12.2 --driver 536.45
```
julia: log excerpt: `kernel timeout on attention_scratch.cu:423` then fallback with 10-20% higher latency.
carlos: pulling telemetry now — matching signals from marketplace images that didn't pin to driver 535.86. Impact estimate: ~1200 requests/day across 6 customers, mostly SI proofs of concept.
maya: high level checklist I propose: 1) vendor hotpatch artifact + validation, 2) AMI/container rebuilds with pinned driver, 3) canary rollout to eu-west-3, 4) partner comms + joint announcement window, 5) rollback playbook.
lee: I'll own vendor engagement and produce a hotpatch artifact (build + minimal test). ETA 3h.
partner-ops: note — some marketplace images are on a curated cadence; we need marketplace approval to push new AMIs. I can fast-track if release notes and validation tests are attached.
carlos: I'll run the canary smoke in eu-west-3 and us-west-2 once we have an artifact. Test plan: 1000 short-seq requests, perf baseline, and CRC of outputs.
sre-bot: deploy-create: canary cluster eu-west-3 scheduled at 2026-03-22T18:40:00Z — id dpl-8421.
julia: Partner comms draft (very short): "We observed a perf regression under a specific driver+cuda combo. We're rolling a hotpatch and rebuilt images; no customer data affected. We recommend pinning drivers to 535.x until the patch is applied." Thoughts?
maya: Good start. Add explicit rollback instructions for customers using air-gapped SI installs: "If you can't apply the patch, revert to driver 535.86 and pin kernel-ABI until we confirm GA."
lee: vendor suggests labeling the artifact `rdi-hotfix-20260322-v1` and publishing a companion diff that documents what changed in kernel calls.
partner-ops: Marketplace ask list: artifacts, smoke test results, signed SBOM, release notes snippet, and contact for partner support. I'll queue the approval request once we have those.
carlos: quick note on validation scripts — use this command for the smoke harness:
```bash
./smoke_harness --endpoint $CANARY_ENDPOINT --requests 1000 --seq 128 --compare-baseline baseline.json
```
carlos: will attach baseline.json and raw latencies to the approval ticket.
maya: For the joint announcement: keep it defensive and technical. Proposed sentence: "Joint hotpatch mitigates a narrow driver interaction causing degraded latency on A100 for short-sequence quantized workloads. Customers should pin to 535.x or apply the hotpatch when available."
julia: agree. Also prep an internal postmortem-lite: timeline, impact, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (long-term: add driver/version gating to AMI builder).
lee: Action owner list:
- lee: vendor fix + artifact (ETA 3h)
- carlos: canary smoke + telemetry (ETA 4h)
- maya: marketplace release notes & announcement draft (ETA 6h)
- partner-ops: approval fast-track + publishing (on signal)
- julia: coord SI customers and assemble PM-lite (ETA 8h)
partner-ops: ping me when smoke results are in. I'll loop in the marketplace PM and legal if language touches joint branding.
sre-bot: alert: canary run completed with 0 regressions in eu-west-3 (2026-03-22T19:05:00Z). Report: s3://redwood-canary-reports/dpl-8421/report.json
carlos: attaching quick summary: median latency improved to baseline, p95 stable. No functional drift. Uploading artifacts now.
maya: I'll wait for the artifacts and then submit the marketplace approval. If approved, we'll schedule AMI/container rollout across regions in a staged window next Monday.
julia: thanks everyone — keep updates here. If we see any customer escalations I'll post them in #support and loop legal for any co-branded comms. :thumbsup:
